title: Bilinear adjunction for the inverse image of a morphism of sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], small relative to the common universe of sheaf values [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sites: its inverse image $L=f^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ is left adjoint to $R=f_*$ and preserves finite limits. Use the induced functors on abelian sheaves and their canonical adjunction, with unit $\eta_F:F\to RLF$, as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For abelian sheaves $F,G$ on $\mathcal C$ and $H$ on $\mathcal D$, let $\operatorname{Bilin}(A\times B,K)$ denote morphisms of underlying sheaves of sets $A\times B\to K$ that are additive separately in each variable on sections over every site object. In the following formula, $R(\beta)$ means the direct image on underlying sheaves of sets; the bilinear map $\beta$ need not be a morphism of abelian sheaves from the product. Using the canonical product identification $R(LF\times LG)\cong RLF\times RLG$, the formula
$$\Theta_{F,G,H}(\beta)=R(\beta)\circ(\eta_F\times\eta_G)$$
defines a bijection
$$\operatorname{Bilin}(LF\times LG,H)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Bilin}(F\times G,RH),$$
natural in $F,G,H$. This asserts the displayed formula for the bijection, not merely existence of a bijection.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality in the proof, specialized to integer-module sheaves; the adjoint of a bilinear map is obtained by composing its direct image with the two units.

proof.text: Work in the sheaf-value universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3), write $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ for the continuous functor defining $f$. Then $R$ is restriction along $u$, so it preserves finite products: on each object $U$, $R(A\times B)(U)=A(uU)\times B(uU)=(RA\times RB)(U)$, and $R(*)$ has singleton sections. Write $\rho_{A,B}:R(A\times B)\to RA\times RB$ for this identification and $\lambda_{A,B}:L(A\times B)\to LA\times LB$ for the canonical comparison, which is invertible by the assumed finite-limit preservation. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects], abelian sheaves are precisely abelian group objects in sheaves of sets, with the sectionwise operations. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-abelian-group-objects] applies to the set adjunction $L\dashv R$. It supplies the group structures $+_{LA}=L(+_A)\lambda_{A,A}^{-1}$ and $+_{RH}=R(+_H)\rho_{H,H}^{-1}$, and says that $\eta_A$ and $\varepsilon_H:L(RH)\to H$ are additive. These are the induced abelian functors and unit specified in the item by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3).

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality: use Sites Section 00YR, Proposition 00YV(2), proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, for the algebraic structures and lifted adjunction.

proof.text:
First ignore all group laws. The ordinary set adjunction and $\lambda_{F,G}$ give inverse bijections on all underlying sheaf maps
$$\Phi(\beta)=R(\beta\lambda_{F,G})\eta_{F\times G},\qquad J(b)=\varepsilon_H L(b)\lambda_{F,G}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $\eta$ with the two projections gives
$$\rho_{LF,LG}R(\lambda_{F,G})\eta_{F\times G}=\eta_F\times\eta_G,$$
since composing either side with each projection gives respectively $\eta_F\mathrm{pr}_1$ and $\eta_G\mathrm{pr}_2$. Therefore $\Phi(\beta)=R(\beta)\rho_{LF,LG}^{-1}(\eta_F\times\eta_G)$, which is exactly the formula required in the item. The inverse formula is the counit formula for the same adjunction, not a new choice of a bijection.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality: ordinary set adjunction, with the product and two-unit normalization written out.

proof.text:
If $\beta$ is separately additive, so is $\Phi(\beta)$. Indeed, for sections $x,x'\in F(U)$ and $y\in G(U)$ its value at $(x+x',y)$ is
$$\beta_{uU}\bigl(\eta_F(x)+\eta_F(x'),\eta_G(y)\bigr)=\beta_{uU}\bigl(\eta_F(x),\eta_G(y)\bigr)+\beta_{uU}\bigl(\eta_F(x'),\eta_G(y)\bigr).$$
Here the component of each $\eta$ is evaluated at $U$, and step 1 gives its additivity. For $y'\in G(U)$ the other additivity equation is
$$\Phi(\beta)_U(x,y+y')=\beta_{uU}\bigl(\eta_F(x),\eta_G(y)+\eta_G(y')\bigr)=\beta_{uU}\bigl(\eta_F(x),\eta_G(y)\bigr)+\beta_{uU}\bigl(\eta_F(x),\eta_G(y')\bigr).$$ The operations on $RH(U)=H(uU)$ are exactly these operations by restriction. Additivity also implies preservation of zero by cancellation, and preservation of negatives by applying additivity to $x+(-x)$ (respectively $y+(-y)$).

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality: forward preservation of separate additivity, expanded on sections.

proof.text:
Conversely let $b:F\times G\to RH$ be separately additive and put $\widetilde b=L(b)\lambda_{F,G}^{-1}:LF\times LG\to L(RH)$. Express its first additivity law before applying $L$ as an equality of sheaf maps from $F\times F\times G$:
$$b\langle +_F\langle p_1,p_2\rangle,p_3\rangle=+_{RH}\langle b\langle p_1,p_3\rangle,b\langle p_2,p_3\rangle\rangle.$$
Apply $L$ to this equality. Identify $L(F\times F\times G)$ with $LF\times LF\times LG$ by its three projection maps, and identify each binary product by $\lambda$. Functoriality preserves composition; for any $q:S\to A$ and $r:S\to B$ the identity
$$\lambda_{A,B}L\langle q,r\rangle=\langle Lq,Lr\rangle$$
follows by composing with each projection, giving $Lq$ and $Lr$. This identity applies to every pairing in the displayed additivity equation. The operation $L(+_F)$ becomes $+_{LF}$ and $L(+_{RH})$ becomes $+_{L(RH)}$ by step 1. Consequently the resulting equality is
$$\widetilde b\langle +_{LF}\langle p_1,p_2\rangle,p_3\rangle=+_{L(RH)}\langle\widetilde b\langle p_1,p_3\rangle,\widetilde b\langle p_2,p_3\rangle\rangle.$$
For the other variable apply $L$ to the analogous equality on $F\times G\times G$,
$$b\langle p_1,+_G\langle p_2,p_3\rangle\rangle=+_{RH}\langle b\langle p_1,p_2\rangle,b\langle p_1,p_3\rangle\rangle.$$
Using $L(+_G)\lambda_{G,G}^{-1}=+_{LG}$ and the pairing identity just proved gives explicitly
$$\widetilde b\langle p_1,+_{LG}\langle p_2,p_3\rangle\rangle=+_{L(RH)}\langle\widetilde b\langle p_1,p_2\rangle,\widetilde b\langle p_1,p_3\rangle\rangle,$$
now on $LF\times LG\times LG$. These equalities of sheaf maps give the claimed identities on every object's sections. Zero and negative identities again follow by cancellation. This calculation uses only finite products and the structure-map formulas of step 1.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality: inverse direction: explicitly transport the two additivity equations by the finite-product comparison.

proof.text: The counit $\varepsilon_H:L(RH)\to H$ is an abelian-sheaf morphism by the lifted-adjunction statement used in step 1. Postcomposing either additivity equality of step 4 with $\varepsilon_H$, and using $\varepsilon_H+_{L(RH)}=+_H(\varepsilon_H\times\varepsilon_H)$, proves that $J(b)=\varepsilon_H\widetilde b$ is separately additive. Thus the mutually inverse bijections $\Phi,J$ of step 2 both restrict to the subsets of bilinear maps. In particular their restrictions are inverse: if $t=\beta\lambda_{F,G}$, then $\varepsilon_H LR(t)L\eta_{F\times G}=t\varepsilon_{L(F\times G)}L\eta_{F\times G}=t$; and for $b$ the other composite is $R\varepsilon_H RL(b)\eta_{F\times G}=R\varepsilon_H\eta_{RH}b=b$. These are counit naturality and the two adjunction triangle identities, with the $\lambda$ and $\lambda^{-1}$ factors cancelling.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality: counit additivity and the two inverse identities.

proof.text:
Finally let $a:F'\to F$, $c:G'\to G$ and $h:H\to H'$ be abelian-sheaf morphisms. Functoriality of $R$, the componentwise description of $\rho$, and unit naturality $RL(a)\eta_{F'}=\eta_F a$ and $RL(c)\eta_{G'}=\eta_G c$ give
$$\Phi_{F',G',H'}\bigl(h\beta(La\times Lc)\bigr)=R(h)\Phi_{F,G,H}(\beta)(a\times c).$$
All these compositions preserve separate additivity because $a,c,h$ and their induced images are additive. This is precisely naturality, contravariantly in $F,G$ and covariantly in $H$. Together with steps 2 and 5 it proves the required natural bijection with its specified two-unit formula.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality: naturality in the two inputs and the output, directly from the specified formula.
